comparison: Both address the central claim about wide TSE with Mg2+ (C4-C6, C28-C32, C59, C62). OpenEval finds the computational evidence SUPPORTED across multiple methods. Peer reviewers rate this UNCERTAIN, stating it 'may be a misinterpretation' and that 'questions still remain about their conclusion regarding the wide-TS.' This represents the most significant disagreement in the evaluations.

Both evaluate activation barrier calculations (C19-C22, C40-C41, C76, C79). OpenEval finds the computational-experimental agreement SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, citing 'large discrepancies between DFTB QM/MM and PBE QM/MM results' and between different computational methods, undermining confidence in specific barrier values.

Both address experimental entropy measurements (C46-C51, C7). OpenEval finds the experimental validation SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the entropy change can be 'attributed sorely to the difference in the reaction geometries near TS' and noting that 'wide conformational ensemble is not a quantitative measure of entropy.' The connection between TSE width and measured entropy is disputed.

Both evaluate pH-dependence experiments validating protonation states (C52-C53, C84-C85). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate this SUPPORTED. Agreement that experimental data validates computational predictions about protonation states.

Both address arginine roles and mutational validation (C37-C39, C56, C69). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate this SUPPORTED. Agreement that computational predictions about active site residues are validated by mutagenesis experiments.
Both evaluate experimental metal ion comparison (C54-C55). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate this SUPPORTED. Agreement that this straightforward kinetic measurement is valid.

Both address geometric/electronic TSE characterization (C24-C27) and mechanistic Mg2+ roles (C33-C35 in peer R4). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED as computational observations. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting these as valid simulation results without challenging the mechanistic details, though interpretation regarding TSE width remains contested elsewhere.
OpenEval R5 addresses mechanistic Mg2+ roles (C33-C36) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R4 includes C33-C35 and rates SUPPORTED. Partial overlap with agreement on mechanistic details from simulations.

OpenEval R11 addresses the central conceptual conclusion about TSE and entropic barriers (C44-C45, C58, C61) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R9 addresses C58 specifically and rates UNSUPPORTED, stating that demonstrating this as a 'catalytic strategy' requires comparison to non-enzymatic reaction that was not performed. Major disagreement on the fundamental claim.

OpenEval R11 includes C44-C45 about TSE-entropy connection rated SUPPORTED. Peer R3 includes C44-C45 rated UNCERTAIN, questioning the interpretation of entropy changes. Disagreement on whether computational TSE width validly explains experimental entropy measurements.

OpenEval R1 includes committor analysis claims (C78, C81-C82) as part of SUPPORTED evidence for wide TSE. Peer R8 rates these UNCERTAIN, noting that concerns about 'large discrepancies' between methods extend to commitment analysis, which depends on validity of underlying free energy surfaces.

OpenEval R10 addresses methodological comparison between computational methods (C79-C80) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes C79 and rates the broader computational methodology UNCERTAIN due to discrepancies between methods. Peer reviewers see the discrepancies as problematic while OpenEval treats the explanation as adequate.

OpenEval R8 addresses computational methodology validation including C76 (higher-level DFT validation) rated SUPPORTED. Peer R2 includes C76 but rates UNCERTAIN due to methodological inconsistencies. Disagreement on whether validation efforts are sufficient.

OpenEval R12 addresses broader implications about TSE concept and enzyme size (C63-C64, C66-C67) rated UNCERTAIN as speculative hypotheses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific speculative claims.
OpenEval R13 addresses evolutionary explanation for rate-limiting lid-opening (C68) rated UNCERTAIN as speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific claim.

OpenEval R14 addresses background information and established knowledge (C1-C3, C8-C18, C23, C42, C70, C72, C83) rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these are contextual claims rather than novel findings requiring evaluation.
OpenEval R15 addresses substrate positioning conclusions (C57) rated SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific structural claim.
